name: Longjia
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Hsiu, Andrew C. 2013 Longjia documentation (cited on Glottolog long1417 page); language extinct and 'poorly attested'

sources.citation: Hölzl, Andreas. 2021. Longjia (China) – Language Contexts. Language Documentation and Description 20, 13-34. DOI 10.25894/LDD29 (CC BY-NC).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the 23-page article (a full-text search for stress/accent/syllab: no hits). Only prosodic remark, p. 24 (sec. 6 'Linguistic ecology'): 'Longjia shares many features with the languages of this area (e.g., a tone system: Pojiao 55, 33, 13, 31), although its typology and areal connections have yet to be explored.' Sec. 7 (pp. 25-30) gives tone-numbered examples (prenasalized onsets, pronouns, numerals) from Zhang & Li's 1982 Pojiao field notes and states the only description is GMSWSB 1982: 22-43; 'Typological and historical descriptions of the language wi…

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2013. New endangered Tibeto-Burman languages of southwestern China: Mondzish, Longjia, Pherbu, and others. Paper presented at ICSTLL 46, Dartmouth College, 8-10 Aug 2013. 24 slides. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1127796.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone. Longjia slides (sec. 3): extinct in the 1970s/80s; ~20 words/phrases written in Chinese characters by Zhao Qiming in 1974 (Jiangyizhai, Anshun); cognate percentages quoted from the 2002 Guizhou Ethnic Gazetteer; a 7-item comparison with Caijia and Bai (Longjia forms given without tone marks); 'Longjia is too poorly attested to classify with certainty.' Zenodo could not be reached by automated download by automated download; downloaded via direct download and copied into the custody folder.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. Longjia page, 'Sino-Tibetan languages' section of msealangs (sites.google.com/site/msealangs/sino-tibetan/languages), fieldwork notes 2013.
sources.note: No linguistic data: reports that the last fluent speakers most likely died in the 1970s, a 99-year-old semi-speaker in Sanjin (Zhijin) had recently died, and that a local researcher Yang Dehua's IPA notes of 'a few hundred Longjia words' are lost.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Longjia language' (accessed 2026-09-17), citing Guizhou Province Gazetteer: Ethnic Gazetteer (贵州省志·民族志, 2002) and Hölzl 2021.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Reports '38 onsets and 22 rimes (8 simple, 14 complex)' and 'many prenasalized onsets' (attributed to the 2002 Gazetteer); four varieties Pojiao (Dafang), Huaxi (Qianxi), Jiangyizhai (Puding), Caiguan (Anshun).

sources.citation: CGZZ 2004 = 白族语言 [Bai language], in 汪波 et al. (eds.), 蔡官镇志 [Caiguan Town Gazetteer], 493-496. Guiyang: 贵州人民出版社.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Three-page phonology and word/phrase sample of the otherwise unknown Caiguan (Xixiu, Anshun) variety of Longjia, labelled 'Bai' (Hölzl 2021: 30); typographically unreliable but the only other phonological sketch.

sources.citation: GMSWSB 1982 = 贵州省民族事务委员会识别办公室. 贵州民族识别资料集 vol. 8: 龙家，蔡家 [Guizhou ethnic identification materials 8: Longjia, Caijia]. Guiyang, unpublished manuscript; Longjia description pp. 22-43 (= Glottolog ref 321403, dated 1986, 136 pp.).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Per Hölzl 2021: 25 'the only description of Longjia' (22 printed pp.: phonology, grammar, lexicon, comparisons); a Chinese 音系 section could carry a remark on 重音 (stress), though such reports rarely do.

sources.citation: Hölzl, Andreas. 2024. Postnominal flagging and OV in Sinitic. Studies in Language. DOI 10.1075/sl.23055.hol.

sources.note: Published (print) summary of the 1980s identification work; source of the '38 onsets, 22 rimes' phonology figures quoted on Wikipedia, so it contains a phonology paragraph that might mention tones/stress.

sources.citation: GMSGL = 贵州省民族识别工作队龙家组. 龙家族属问题调查报告 [Report on the ethnic affiliation of the Longjia]. Unpublished handwritten manuscript, 46 pp., after 1986; related to Glottolog ref 319430, 南龙人（南京-龙家）族别问题调查报告 (1984, 54 pp.).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Handwritten variant of the 1982 description with phonetic transcriptions (Hölzl 2021: 16, 25); same content class as GMSWSB 1982.

sources.citation: Zhang Jimin 张济民 & Li Juewei 李珏伟. 1982. 语言调查大纲: 大方龙家语 [Language survey outline: Dafang Longjia]. Unpublished handwritten field notes, ~175 pp. (Pojiao, Dafang; speaker Xie Yongxiu, 83). Private copy of Andreas Hölzl, 'currently being prepared for publication' (Hölzl 2021: 31).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only substantial primary record of the language (phonology incl. tones, grammar, hundreds of words); Hölzl's announced typological/phonological description based on it would be the place any stress remark could appear.
